reference_use.conclusion:
SNAPSHOT. Project d8d46c95 and Mathlib 25730c7c hold the frozen Ch06 contract. It defines flatDistance as a three-fold iInf over R, S and the integer-multiplicity/decomposition proof, with summand S.massOn W + R.massOn W, and CompactlyContainedOpen.

LIBRARIES. SimonGMT supplies massAdmissibleOn, massOn, le_massOn, covectorEuclideanNorm_{zero,nonneg}, exteriorDerivativeTestOn, tsupport_exteriorDerivative_subset and GeometricCurrentOn.boundary_apply. It has no mass inequality |T(ω)| ≤ M_W(T)·sup|ω| and no sup-bound lemma for test forms (no match). Mathlib supplies exists_open_between_and_isCompact_closure, ENNReal.tendsto_atTop_zero, Continuous.bounded_above_of_compact_support, HasCompactSupport.comp_left and ContinuousEvalConst for continuous alternating maps.

REUSABLE DECLARATIONS. The DAG holds 200 nodes against max_nodes 200, so no fresh child can be activated. Two comparator-accepted declarations cover Steps 1–3: cmb_abs_apply_le_of_massOn_le (ba202ac0) and cmb_exists_compactly_contained_exhaustion (cb89cc7f). The only other matching type, br_la_testForm_covectorNorm_bounded, is unaccepted under another parent and cannot be shared.

rationale:
DECISION. Split into 2 children, both reusing comparator-accepted declarations by name with byte-identical frozen Lean types. No new DAG node is created. The children have no sibling dependencies.

WHY SPLIT. Apart from bookkeeping, the supplied proof has three ingredients:
- (A) the basic mass estimate (Steps 1–2);
- (B) an open W ⊂⊂ U with tsupport ω ⊆ W (Step 3);
- (C) a near-optimal flat decomposition and the ε-estimate (Steps 4–6).
(A) and (B) are genuine, reusable obligations. Each is already kernel-checked and comparator-accepted in branch root.compactness_mass_bounds-a1:
- mass_bound = Submission.cmb_abs_apply_le_of_massOn_le (candidate ba202ac0). It is also reused by root.integrality_weak_limits-a1.restriction_limit-a1.
- exhaustion = Submission.cmb_exists_compactly_contained_exhaustion (candidate cb89cc7f). It is also reused by the weighted_tangent_ae, mass_measure_representation and restriction_theory branches.
Reuse takes the most technical inline part out of the parent's single-theorem proof: homogeneity of covectorEuclideanNorm and the limit c ↓ C, about 50 Lean lines in the accepted proof. Accepted mathematics is not re-proved.

NODE BUDGET.
- The live swarm config (.humanize/swarm-configs/d0b85dc8….json) has max_nodes = 200, and dag.json holds 200 nodes.
- runtime.py _solve_children computes remaining = max_nodes − |nodes| = 0 and rejects any split that needs a fresh node.
- Reused accepted names resolve through existing_by_name to their existing nodes and need no slot.
- _existing_lean_name_problem allows sharing an accepted checkpoint whose stripped frozen type is identical.
- store.ensure returns the existing node unchanged. _install_parent_supplied_child_handoff and _workspace_payload skip reused accepted children.
So only a reuse-only split can activate. A fresh child for the test-form sup bound is therefore impossible. The identical type br_la_testForm_covectorNorm_bounded cannot be shared either, because it is still decomposing under another parent. That step stays inline in the parent. If a budget existed, a test-form sup-bound lemma and a flat-distance evaluation estimate would have been natural extra children.

HOW THE CHILDREN IMPLY THE SELECTED PARENT BY THE SUPPLIED PROOF.
(i) Step 2 is used only in Step 5, for X ∈ {R_j, S_j}, whose masses M_W(X) are finite by Step 4, and Step 5 reads it in ℝ. The resulting inequality |X(η)| ≤ M_W(X)·C is exactly mass_bound with:
- B := M_W(X).toReal ≥ 0, where M_W(X) ≤ ofReal B because the mass is finite;
- C any pointwise bound for |η|; the parent uses C := max(sup|ω|, sup|dω|);
- tsupport η ⊆ W.
Step 1 is used only inside Step 2's proof, so the child subsumes it.
(ii) Step 3 needs W ⊂⊂ U with tsupport ω ⊆ W. Let K := tsupport ω. K is compact because ω has compact support, and K ⊆ U because ω ∈ D^n(U). Property (b) of exhaustion gives i with K ⊆ W_i, and property (a) gives CompactlyContainedOpen W_i U. Also tsupport dω ⊆ tsupport ω ⊆ W_i by tsupport_exteriorDerivative_subset. This replaces the thickening construction.
(iii) These remain inline in the parent:
- the finiteness of sup|ω| and sup|dω| (the Notation paragraph): x ↦ |η(x)| is continuous and compactly supported;
- Step 4: iInf_lt_iff applied to the three nested infima (R, S, proof) gives the decomposition, and M_W(S_j) + M_W(R_j) < ofReal δ makes both masses finite;
- Step 5: |T_j ω − T ω| = |R_j(dω) + S_j(ω)| ≤ (M_W(R_j).toReal + M_W(S_j).toReal)·C;
- Step 6: the conclusion, with δ := ε/(C+1).

LEAN CHECK.
- The frozen commit d8d46c9 was built in /tmp/ftw-decomp-scratch: a git archive with .lake/packages symlinked to the shared pinned tree. Its Contract sha256 ea3ee0dd… equals the snapshot's.
- The three exact types elaborate as comparator NodeChallenge modules, generated by gmt-compare.py contract_scope/child_modules after validate_lean_statement. The only sorry is the intended placeholder.
- Scratch/AssemblyExact.lean contains both accepted child proofs, copied verbatim from candidates ba202ac0 and cb89cc7f, plus a sorry-free proof of Submission.fiw_flat_to_weak. That proof uses only these two declarations, SimonGMT and Mathlib.
- _root_.HumanizeNodeComparator.target{,_mass_bound,_exhaustion} : (exact frozen type) := by exact Submission.<name> all check. #print axioms lists only [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound].

NO OTHER NODE IS SOLVED. Both children are pre-existing accepted theorems. The parent's remaining argument is specific to this node, and the siblings fiw_localization, fiw_total_boundedness and fiw_flat_cauchy_limit are untouched.

subproblems.title: Mass estimate |T(ω)| ≤ M_W(T)·sup|ω| for test forms supported in W
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U W : Set (Eucl P)) (T : GeometricCurrentOn U n) (ω : TestFormOn U n) (B C : ℝ), 0 ≤ B → T.massOn W ≤ ENNReal.ofReal B → tsupport (ω : DifferentialForm (Eucl P) n) ⊆ W → (∀ x, covectorEuclideanNorm ((ω : DifferentialForm (Eucl P) n) x) ≤ C) → |T ω| ≤ B * C
subproblems.natural_proof:
Reuse note.
- This child is the comparator-accepted declaration Submission.cmb_abs_apply_le_of_massOn_le of DAG node root.compactness_mass_bounds-a1.mass_bound-a1 (status accepted, candidate ba202ac0407b6e93210594416fcd0729874b2eff).
- It is reused by name with the byte-identical frozen Lean type, so no new DAG node is created.
- In the selected parent proof (root.flat_iff_weak-a1.flat_to_weak-a1) it replaces Steps 1–2. Step 5 applies it twice, with C₀ := max(sup|ω|, sup|dω|):
  - (T, ω, B, C) := (R_j, dω, M_W(R_j).toReal, C₀);
  - (T, ω, B, C) := (S_j, ω, M_W(S_j).toReal, C₀).
  Both masses are finite by Step 4, so M_W(·) ≤ ENNReal.ofReal(M_W(·).toReal).
- The 'Source' line below refers to that declaration's original parent, root.compactness_mass_bounds-a1. Its accepted proof is reproduced verbatim.

Source: parent proof Step 2 (basic mass estimate). It is stated with an explicit real bound B for M_W(T) and an explicit pointwise bound C for |ω|, which avoids dividing by sup|ω| and any case distinction on ω = 0.

Notation: for an n-covector α, |α| := covectorEuclideanNorm α = (Σ_{I : Fin n → Fin P, I strictly increasing} α(e_{I(0)},…,e_{I(n−1)})²)^{1/2}, where e_i = EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin P) ℝ i. M_W(T) = T.massOn W is the supremum of ENNReal.ofReal(T(ψ)) over ψ ∈ massAdmissibleOn U n W = {ψ ∈ TestFormOn U n : tsupport ψ ⊆ W and |ψ(x)| ≤ 1 for all x}.

1. (Homogeneity.) For t ∈ ℝ and a covector α, |tα| = |t|·|α|. Each coefficient satisfies (tα)(e_I) = t·α(e_I), so the sum of squares is multiplied by t², and √(t²S) = |t|·√S.
2. (C ≥ 0.) 0 ≤ |ω(0)| ≤ C.
3. (Admissible rescalings.) Fix a real c > C, so c > 0. Let s ∈ {c⁻¹, −c⁻¹}. TestFormOn U n is a real submodule, so s•ω ∈ TestFormOn U n. Also tsupport(s•ω) ⊆ tsupport ω ⊆ W, and by Step 1, |(s•ω)(x)| = c⁻¹|ω(x)| ≤ C/c ≤ 1 for every x. Hence s•ω ∈ massAdmissibleOn U n W, and GeometricCurrentOn.le_massOn gives ENNReal.ofReal(T(s•ω)) ≤ M_W(T) ≤ ENNReal.ofReal B.
4. (Unpacking.) Because B ≥ 0, ENNReal.ofReal a ≤ ENNReal.ofReal B implies a ≤ B (ENNReal.ofReal_le_ofReal_iff). By linearity T(s•ω) = s·T(ω). Therefore c⁻¹T(ω) ≤ B and −c⁻¹T(ω) ≤ B. Multiplying by c > 0 gives T(ω) ≤ Bc and −T(ω) ≤ Bc, i.e. |T(ω)| ≤ B·c. This holds for every c > C.
5. (Letting c ↓ C.) Let ε > 0 and c := C + ε/(B+1) > C. Step 4 gives |T(ω)| ≤ BC + Bε/(B+1) ≤ BC + ε. Since ε > 0 is arbitrary, |T(ω)| ≤ B·C (le_of_forall_pos_le_add). ∎
proof_key_steps: For c > C, ±c⁻¹ω is mass-admissible for W, so ±c⁻¹T(ω) ≤ B by le_massOn and B ≥ 0.
Hence |T(ω)| ≤ B·c for every c > C; let c decrease to C.

subproblems.title: Exhaustion of an open set by compactly contained open sets
subproblems.statement: For every P ∈ ℕ and every open set U ⊆ ℝ^P (= Eucl P) there is a sequence (W_i)_{i∈ℕ} of subsets of ℝ^P with two properties. (a) For every i, CompactlyContainedOpen W_i U holds: W_i is open, closure(W_i) is compact and closure(W_i) ⊆ U. (b) Every compact K ⊆ U is contained in W_i for some i.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P : ℕ) (U : Set (Eucl P)), IsOpen U → ∃ W : ℕ → Set (Eucl P), (∀ i, CompactlyContainedOpen (W i) U) ∧ ∀ K : Set (Eucl P), IsCompact K → K ⊆ U → ∃ i, K ⊆ W i
subproblems.natural_proof:
Reuse note.
- This child is the comparator-accepted declaration Submission.cmb_exists_compactly_contained_exhaustion of DAG node root.compactness_mass_bounds-a1.exhaustion-a1 (status accepted, candidate cb89cc7f436bbfa9b474f73003fa9aa79ebad102).
- It is reused by name with the byte-identical frozen Lean type, so no new DAG node is created.
- In the selected parent proof (root.flat_iff_weak-a1.flat_to_weak-a1) it replaces the thickening construction of Step 3. Let K := tsupport ω; K is compact because ω has compact support, and K ⊆ U because ω ∈ D^n(U). Then:
  - property (b) gives i with K ⊆ W_i;
  - property (a) gives CompactlyContainedOpen W_i U;
  - tsupport dω ⊆ tsupport ω ⊆ W_i by tsupport_exteriorDerivative_subset.
- The 'Source' line below refers to that declaration's original parent, root.compactness_mass_bounds-a1. Its accepted proof is reproduced verbatim.

Source: parent proof Step 1 (exhaustion). The parent's condition B̄_{1/i}(x) ⊆ U is expressed here through the extended distance to ℝ^P∖U, so no convention for dist(x, ∅) is needed. The index is shifted to avoid 1/0.

Notation: |x| is the Euclidean norm on ℝ^P = Eucl P. For x ∈ ℝ^P let d(x) := inf{edist(x, y) : y ∈ ℝ^P∖U} ∈ [0, ∞] (Lean: Metric.infEDist x Uᶜ). If U = ℝ^P then d ≡ ∞.

1. d is continuous (Metric.continuous_infEDist). Since ℝ^P∖U is closed (U is open), d(x) = 0 iff x ∈ closure(ℝ^P∖U) = ℝ^P∖U (Metric.mem_closure_iff_infEDist_zero). In particular d(x) > 0 for every x ∈ U.
2. For i ∈ ℕ define W_i := {x : |x| < i} ∩ {x : (i+1)⁻¹ < d(x)}, where (i+1)⁻¹ ∈ (0, ∞).
3. W_i is open: it is the intersection of the preimages of the open sets (−∞, i) and ((i+1)⁻¹, ∞] under the continuous maps x ↦ |x| and d.
4. W_i ⊆ B̄_i(0), and B̄_i(0) is closed, so closure(W_i) ⊆ B̄_i(0). B̄_i(0) is compact because ℝ^P is proper, so closure(W_i) is compact as a closed subset of a compact set.
5. F_i := {x : (i+1)⁻¹ ≤ d(x)} is closed (d is continuous) and contains W_i, so closure(W_i) ⊆ F_i. Suppose some x ∈ closure(W_i) is not in U. Then d(x) = 0 by Step 1, while x ∈ F_i gives d(x) ≥ (i+1)⁻¹ > 0 (since i+1 < ∞), a contradiction. Hence closure(W_i) ⊆ U. Together with Steps 3 and 4, CompactlyContainedOpen W_i U holds for every i.
6. Let K ⊆ U be compact. If K = ∅ then K ⊆ W_0. Otherwise:
- K is bounded, so there is R ∈ ℝ with |x| ≤ R for all x ∈ K. Choose i₁ ∈ ℕ with i₁ > R.
- d is continuous and K is compact and nonempty, so d attains its minimum on K at some x₀ ∈ K (IsCompact.exists_isMinOn). Since x₀ ∈ U, Step 1 gives m := d(x₀) > 0.
- Choose i₂ ∈ ℕ with (i₂)⁻¹ < m (ENNReal.exists_inv_nat_lt).
- Put i := max(i₁, i₂). For x ∈ K we have |x| ≤ R < i₁ ≤ i and (i+1)⁻¹ ≤ (i₂)⁻¹ < m ≤ d(x), so x ∈ W_i. Hence K ⊆ W_i.
7. Steps 5 and 6 show that (W_i)_{i∈ℕ} has both required properties. ∎
proof_key_steps: d(x) := infEDist(x, ℝ^P∖U) is continuous and vanishes exactly off U.
closure W_i ⊆ closedBall(0,i) ∩ {d ≥ (i+1)⁻¹}, which is compact and contained in U.
A compact K ⊆ U is bounded and min_K d > 0, so K ⊆ W_i for large i.
